introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
incertitudes: Points imprimés 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, conformes au total. (c) : plusieurs réponses admissibles (coke, charbon) ; coke retenu comme réponse principale.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is allotropy?

(ii) Name two allotropes of carbon and give one physical difference between the two allotropes. - Allotropes: ......... - Difference: ......... *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Allotropy is the existence of an element in **two or more different forms in the same physical state**, the forms differing in the arrangement of their atoms (and so in physical properties) but having the same chemical properties.

(ii) **Allotropes:** diamond and graphite.

**Difference:** diamond is very hard whereas graphite is soft and slippery; also graphite conducts electricity while diamond does not (diamond is transparent and sparkling, graphite is dark grey and opaque).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide are two oxides of carbon.

(i) Identify a compound that will react with dilute hydrochloric acid to give carbon dioxide.

(ii) Using an equation only, show how carbon dioxide is converted to carbon monoxide.

(iii) Briefly describe the chemical test that is used to distinguish between carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide.

(iv) Give one industrial use of carbon dioxide. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Any carbonate or hydrogencarbonate, for example **calcium carbonate**: $\mathrm{CaCO_3} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCl_2} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$.

(ii) Passing carbon dioxide over red-hot carbon (coke): $\mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}$.

(iii) Bubble each gas separately through **lime water** (calcium hydroxide solution). Carbon dioxide turns it **milky (cloudy)** because white insoluble calcium carbonate forms: $\mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCO_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. Carbon monoxide has **no effect** on lime water (it burns with a blue flame instead).

(iv) Any one of: making fizzy (carbonated) drinks, fire extinguishers, refrigerant as dry ice (solid $\mathrm{CO_2}$), making washing soda or urea.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the form of carbon that is used as an industrial fuel. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Coke** (also acceptable: coal or charcoal). Coke is burnt as an industrial fuel, for example in blast furnaces.
